title: Clothes for the road (Genesis 3:21–24)
hookLine: before they leave the garden, God makes them garments, a first act of care

lines: A COAT ZIPPED UP AT THE DOOR.
ONE MORE SCENE IN THE GARDEN.
cards: Think of the last time someone you love left home: a kid off to college, a parent heading into surgery. Maybe there were hard words.

And still, at the door, you zipped up their coat, or pressed a sandwich into their hands. Week five, brothers and floods, opens with one more garden scene, and it's easy to miss. The humans are about to be sent out.
And God does something quietly, with the hands.

teach.b: The garden story ends with consequences. The ground will be hard to work, life will involve pain, and the two of them must leave. But right before they go comes a single verse.
In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation: "And the LORD God made for Adam and for his wife garments of skins, and clothed them." Their fig leaves were a patch job.
Now God makes real clothes, the kind that last, and dresses them, like a parent dressing a child.
Then they're sent out, and the way back is guarded by cherubim and a flaming, turning sword. The door closes. But nobody leaves the garden naked.
The rabbis built a whole ethic on that verse. The Torah says to walk after God. How, the Talmud asks?

teach.h: AS GOD CLOTHED, SO SHOULD YOU.
teach.b: As God clothed the naked, clothing Adam and Eve, so should you. As God visited the sick, visiting Abraham, so should you. As God comforted mourners and buried the dead, so should you.
And the Talmud notices that the Torah begins with kindness, clothing people, and ends with it, God burying Moses. Kindness is the frame the whole book sits in. One more detail.
The Hebrew for skin, or, sounds exactly like the word for light. The midrash remembers that Rabbi Meir's own Torah scroll spelled it with the other letter: garments of light.
Either way, what goes out of the garden with them isn't only punishment. It's care.

how: Jewish tradition counts clothing the needy, visiting the sick, comforting mourners and burying the dead among the acts of lovingkindness, gemilut chasadim, understood as walking in God's ways.

o: the clothes God made for Adam and Eve to wear
guardians blocking the way back into the garden
angels who sang to Adam and Eve in the garden

games.q: as God did, so should you — tap the pairs.

s: Adam and Eve leave the garden wearing fig leaves
God makes them garments of skins and dresses them before they go.
the Talmud says the Torah begins and ends with kindness
clothing Adam and Eve at the start; burying Moses at the end.
the garden story ends only in punishment
right before they leave, God clothes them: care goes with them.

games.q: the Torah says to walk after God. you're a rabbi of the Talmud. how can a person walk after God?
o: climb a mountain to be closer.
follow God's ways: clothe, visit, comfort, bury.
games.why: as God clothed the naked, so should you; as God visited the sick, comforted mourners and buried the dead, so should you.

practice: Bring to mind someone who is leaving something right now: a job, a home, a hospital, a stage of life, even if it ended badly.
Picture them at the door, and one small, practical thing you could put in their hands for the road: a meal, a ride, a note. Stay with them there for a few slow breaths.

wordCard.voice: Cherubim, the guardian beings with a flaming sword at the garden's gate. Adam and Eve go out past them already dressed, in garments made by God's own hands.

orig.note: Hebrew: garments of skin. or, skin, sounds like or, light, spelled with a different first letter.

carryVoice: Your line: care goes with you. Tomorrow, the first brothers: Cain and Abel. See you then.
